questions.text: How can you say that the Lok Sabha has more authority over financial matters?
questions.text_as_printed: How can you say that the Lok Sabha has more authority over financial matters? (D)

answer.value:
Financial Powers and Functions of Parliament
Parliament has complete control over the nation’s finances.
The government cannot collect taxes or spend money without Parliament’s approval.
Financial bills must first be introduced in the Lok Sabha.
After approval by the Lok Sabha, the bill is sent to the Rajya Sabha.
The Rajya Sabha must return the bill with its approval within 14 days; otherwise, it is considered approved by Financial Powers and Functions of Parliament

questions.text: Explain the powers and functions of Parliament in amending the Constitution.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the powers and functions of Parliament in amending the Constitution. (A)

answer.value:
Parliament’s Powers and Functions to Amend the Constitution
Under Article 368 of the Indian Constitution, Parliament has the authority to amend the Constitution.
A Constitution Amendment Bill can be introduced in either house of Parliament.
The bill requires separate approval from both houses of Parliament.
If one house rejects the bill approved by the other, the amendment cannot proceed.
In some cases, the approval of half of the state legislatures is also required for a Constitution Amendment Bill passed by Parliament.

questions.text: Analyze the financial powers and functions of the President.
questions.text_as_printed: Analyze the financial powers and functions of the President. (D)

answer.value:
Financial Powers and Functions of the President
A financial bill cannot be introduced in the Lok Sabha without the President’s prior approval.
The President recommends discussion in Parliament of reports from the Central Finance Commission, the Comptroller and Auditor General, and the Controller of Accounts.
The Consolidated Fund of India and the Contingency Fund are under the President’s control.
Salaries for Supreme Court judges, the Chairperson, and members of the Union Public Service Commission are disbursed from these funds.
The President’s approval is required for a financial bill to become an act.

Returning a bill passed by Parliament for reconsideration.

questions.text: Explain the executive powers and functions of Parliament.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the executive powers and functions of Parliament. (A)

answer.value:
Executive Powers and Functions of Parliament
India follows a parliamentary system of government.
The Council of Ministers, led by the Prime Minister, is the real executive.
The Council of Ministers is accountable to Parliament.
Parliament exercises complete control over the executive by questioning the Council of Ministers.
The Council of Ministers can continue in office as long as it enjoys the confidence of the Lok Sabha.
If the Lok Sabha passes a no-confidence motion, the Council of Ministers must resign.

The President also has the constitutional authority to remove such appointees.

questions.text: Explain the legislative powers and functions of Parliament.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the legislative powers and functions of Parliament. (A)

answer.value:
Legislative Powers and Functions of Parliament
Parliament is fundamentally a law-making body.
It has the authority to legislate on subjects listed in the Union List, such as finance, defense, aerospace, telecommunications, railways, foreign affairs, and nuclear energy.
Ordinary bills can be introduced in either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha.
For a bill to become law, it must be approved by both houses through discussions.
In case of a tie in votes, the Speaker casts the deciding vote.
If there is a disagreement between the two houses, the President can call a joint session of Parliament to resolve it.
Once approved by both houses, the bill is sent to the President for assent.
Upon the President’s approval, the bill becomes an act.

questions.text: Mention the legislative powers and functions of the President.
questions.text_as_printed: Mention the legislative powers and functions of the President. (A)

answer.value:
Legislative Powers and Functions of the President
The President has the authority to summon, prorogue, address, and dissolve the Lok Sabha.
The President can address a joint session of both houses of Parliament.
Bills passed by both houses of Parliament require the President’s assent, or they may be returned for reconsideration or rejected without signing.
Prior to 2020, the President had the authority to nominate two Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha.
The 104th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2020 discontinued this nomination.
The President can nominate 12 individuals who have distinguished themselves in arts, science, social service, or literature to the Rajya Sabha.
The President exercises these powers on the advice of the Council of Ministers led by the Prime Minister.

questions.text: Explain the formation and responsibilities of the Central Council of Ministers.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the formation and responsibilities of the Central Council of Ministers. (D)

answer.value:
Formation and Responsibilities of the Central Council of Ministers
Article 74(1) of the Constitution mandates a Council of Ministers led by the Prime Minister to aid and advise the President.
The Central Council of Ministers, led by the Prime Minister, is the real executive and manages the entire administration of the nation.
The Council formulates and implements public policies and programs.
The Council of Ministers is categorized into three types: Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers.
The Council is collectively responsible to Parliament (Lok Sabha) for its administration, policy decisions, and programs.
The Council remains in office as long as it enjoys the confidence of the Lok Sabha.
The Lok Sabha can remove the Council of Ministers by passing a no-confidence motion.
